messages.subject: How to obtain a submatrix
parts:
Dear Stan users.

After reading the stan-reference and some posts in this group, I don't know how to delete the row and column of a given element of a matrix.
I understand the function block, but I think it's not enough for my problem.

For instance, imagine you have a 4 by 4 matrix

      | 1 2 1 1 | 
A = | 2 8 2 2 |
      | 3 2 3 3 |
      | 4 2 4 4 |

aand you want to delete the row and column of the element 8, i.e., delete the second row and the second column. Then, by using the elements which are not deleted
we could create a new 3 by 3 matrix:


      |1 1 1|
B = |3 3 3|
      |4 4 4|


Furthermore, for the elements 8 and 9 in the following matrix, whill imply to delete several rows and columns:

      | 1 2 3 1 | 
A = | 2 8 3 2 |
      | 3 2 9 3 |
      | 4 2 3 4 |

      |1 1 |
B = |4 4 |

In my problem the elements always belong to the diagonal.

Thanks in advance.
Angel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to obtain a submatrix
parts:
There's no built-in way to do that. You have to write
the loops yourself. If you want to get rid of row and
column n in an N x N matrix, then you can do it one
quadrant at a time, as so:

matrix delete_row_col(matrix a, int n) {
matrix[rows(a) - 1, cols(a) - 1] result;
for (i in 1:(n-1)) {
for (j in 1:(n-1))
result[i,j] <- a[i,j];
for (j in (n+1):N)
result[i,j-1] <- a[i,j];
}
for (i in (n+1):N) {
for (j in 1:(n-1))
result[i-1,j] <- a[i,j];
for (j in (n+1):N)
result[i-1,j-1] <- a[i,j];
}
return result;
}

Of course, if you don't know the row/col, then you need to write
another loop to find that first. And if you have more than one match,
then the function gets trickier, but you could reduce it to removing
one at a time.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to obtain a submatrix
parts:
I'm not sure what you mean. Positions (indexes?) in
matrices aren't real numbers.

You're right that Stan does not automatically demote reals
to integers --- in that way it's like Java, not like C/C++.

> For instance, imagine you have a 4 by 4 matrix
> >
> > | 1 2 1 1 |
> > A = | 2 8 2 2 |
> > | 3 2 3 3 |
> > | 4 2 4 4 |
> >
> > and you want to delete the row and column of the element 8, i.e., delete the second row and the second column.

Assuming this example reflects what you want to do, you
need to write a function to find the index:

int diagonal_index_of(matrix x, real y) {
for (i in 1:rows(x))
if (x[i,i] == y) return i;
return -1;
}

Then just plug the index into the other function. Or put
them together into a single function.

- Bob

messages.author: fee73ca0c556eec2
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to obtain a submatrix
parts:
Hi Bob! Sorry, I forgot to say "thank you very much"

Finally, I used your answer to obtain what I wanted (below): a block_multi_normal_log

Cheers!
Angel


functions{
matrix extract_block_matrix(matrix a, row_vector indicator, int n_elements) {
  int aux_n;
  int aux_m;
  matrix[rows(a), cols(a)- n_elements] aux_result;
  matrix[rows(a)- n_elements,rows(a)- n_elements] result;
#
  aux_m <- 1;
  for(j in 1:cols(a)){
    if(indicator[j] == 0){
      for(i in 1:rows(a))
        aux_result[i,aux_m] <- a[i,j];
        aux_m <- aux_m + 1;
    }
  }
  aux_n <- 1;
  for(n in 1:rows(aux_result)){
    if(indicator[n] == 0){
      for(m in 1:cols(aux_result)){
        result[aux_n,m] <- aux_result[n,m];
      }
    aux_n <- aux_n +1;
    }
  }
  return result;
}
#
row_vector extract_block_vector(row_vector x, row_vector indicator, int n_elements) {
  int aux_n;
  row_vector[cols(x)- n_elements] result;
  aux_n <- 1;
  for(j in 1:cols(x)){
    if(indicator[j] == 0){
      result[aux_n] <- x[j];
      aux_n <- aux_n +1;
      }
  }
  return result;
}
#
real block_multi_normal_log(row_vector y, row_vector x, matrix a, row_vector indicator, int n_elements ){
  row_vector[cols(x)- n_elements] y_vector;
  row_vector[cols(x)- n_elements] mu;
  matrix[rows(a)- n_elements,rows(a)- n_elements] Sigma;

  y_vector <- extract_block_vector(y,indicator,n_elements);
  mu <- extract_block_vector(x,indicator,n_elements);
  Sigma <- extract_block_matrix(a,indicator,n_elements);
  return multi_normal_log(to_vector(y_vector), to_vector(mu), Sigma);

}

}
